description:
pkix-ct/src/log_list.rs:56 — #[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)] on CtLogList. CtLog itself derives PartialEq + Eq + Hash. The inner BTreeMap<[u8;32], CtLog> supports PartialEq + Eq (Hash is not auto-derived for BTreeMap, but that's fine).

Per workspace non-negotiable #6 ('Cache-friendly result types ... MUST derive Clone + Debug + PartialEq + Eq ... and SHOULD support serde::Serialize + Deserialize behind a serde feature flag for cross-process / persistent caches'): CtLogList is configuration that callers will want to compare ('did the log list change since I cached this verdict?'), serialize (for cross-process caches), and dedup. Currently:
- No PartialEq → cannot test equality.
- No Eq → cannot use as HashMap key.
- No serde → cannot persist to disk in caller-side caches without bespoke conversion.

CtLog already derives PartialEq/Eq/Hash. The CtLogList wrapper needlessly drops them. Suggested fix: add PartialEq + Eq to the derive list. Add an optional serde Serialize/Deserialize behind a feature flag (probably 'serde' as a cross-cutting feature, matching the pattern in pkix-path).

Concrete user scenario: a caller writes a CT validation cache keyed by (cert_id, log_list_fingerprint). Today they have to hash the underlying BTreeMap manually or compute a fingerprint by iterating CtLogList::iter(). Trivial fix unblocks a documented design intent.
title: CtLogList drops PartialEq/Eq derives, blocking caller-side dedup and prevalidation caches
